thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered for service=hosted-inference-prod severity=P1. Summary: spike in 503 error rate across us-east-*. Assigned to: Alice (primary). If no ack in 5m -> escalate to Bob (secondary). Incident link: https://pd.example.com/incidents/INC-9923
Alice (oncall): acked. I'm on it. Starting with logs and metrics.
Alice (oncall): quick note — seeing 503s primarily from inference-shard-7 behind the regional LB.  p50 latencies normal, error rate up to 14% for last 6m.
Alice (oncall): paging @Bob for backup if this needs cross-team bridge.
Bob (secondary): I see the PD page but haven't fully dug in yet. On a call, will join the thread in ~4m.
incident-bot: Reminder: auto-escalation to manager in 1m if no ack from secondary.
Alice (oncall): running a rolling restart on shard-7 now: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-shard-7 -n prod` — will post logs.
Dave (SRE): heads-up — scaling rules recently changed yesterday; autoscaler might have a cooldown. Check `cluster-autoscaler` events.
Alice (oncall): restart started. Logs show repeated:
```
ERROR http: upstream returned 503 "model timeout"
stack: runtime/gc? worker timed out after 2500ms
```
Guessing model runtime exhaustion or queueing.
incident-bot: PagerDuty escalation: secondary (Bob) did not ACK within 5m. Escalating to manager Carol.
Carol (manager): got escalated. I'm awake. Are you requesting that I take the bridge or should I let oncall continue?
Alice (oncall): thanks Carol. Restart did reduce errors on a few pods but 503s persist. I recommend we open a brief bridge and consider scaling the inference pool and throttling low-priority tenants.
Emma (support): We're already getting customer reports in Zendesk — I see 9 tickets so far referencing 503s from API. Triage label added: `inc-usc-503`.
Bob (secondary): I'm on the bridge now (joining). Sorry for delay, was finishing a deploy.
Carol (manager): ok please take lead on mitigation with Alice. If this is scheduler-related and we need infra quota, escalate to infra. I'll notify SOC for a customer status update if we have impact > 10 customers.
Bob (secondary): quick check — kernel OOMs on a different node in the cluster earlier around 3350004200, but not sure related. I'm going to pin to model-workers and restart queue processes. Running:
```
for pod in $(kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=inference-shard-7 -o name); do kubectl -n prod exec $pod -- supervisorctl restart queue; done
```
Alice (oncall): applied a 2x temporary scale to inference-pool-us-east and enabled `prefix_kv_cache` for that deployment to reduce model compute. Monitoring.
Dave (SRE): I'm increasing LB healthcheck timeout from 2s -> 5s as a short-term mitigation (will revert after). Applied via: `terraform apply -var region=us-east -target=module.lb.healthcheck`
incident-bot: PagerDuty note: manager escalation triggered due to missed secondary ack. Carol was paged at 3350004401.
Alice (oncall): error rate trending down to ~3% now. Customer reports are still trickling in but no new surge.
Emma (support): updated customers with a preliminary note: "We're investigating intermittent 503s in us-east; mitigation in progress. We'll update in 30m."
Bob (secondary): confirmed queue restarts cleared backlog on two pods. No more repeated `model timeout` entries after restarts.
Carol (manager): thanks team. Keep monitoring. Capture post-incident notes: root cause candidate: surge in queued requests causing worker-side timeouts after autoscaler cooldown; contributing factor: recent scaling rule change. Action items: 1) revert risky scaling tweak if confirmed, 2) add PD runbook step for immediate pool bump + queue restart, 3) owners: infra/SRE + runtime.
Alice (oncall): I'll open INC-9923-PR with logs+timelines and draft RCA.
Bob (secondary): will follow up with a runbook patch for `supervisorctl restart queue` and add a k8s liveness probe tweak.
Carol (manager): I'll author the customer follow-up and coordinate postmortem. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident status changed to "Mitigated". Auto-close in 6h if no regression.
Alice (oncall): marking this thread closed for now, will add notes to the incident ticket later.
Emma (support): will keep tickets updated.
Carol (manager): last_message: good job. Please add timelines and affected customer list to the RCA.
